'''Okinohata Suitengu''' (沖端水天宮) is a {{ill|Suitengū|en|Suitengū|qid=Q125319456|lt=Shinto Shrine (Suitengu)|1=Suitengū}} located in Inari Town, {{ill|Yanagawa, Fukuoka|en|Yanagawa, Fukuoka|qid=Q585630|lt=Yanagawa City|1=Yanagawa, Fukuoka}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}. The registered {{ill|Civil registration|en|Civil registration|qid=Q83708009|lt=Registration|1=Civil registration}} name under the {{ill|Religious Corporation|ja|宗教法人|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious Corporation|1=religious corporation|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q7311343}} is '''Suitengu''' (すいてんぐう).
== 祭神 ==
* {{ill|Emperor Antoku|en|Emperor Antoku|qid=Q316651|lt=Emperor Antoku|1=Emperor Antoku}}
== 由緒 ==
{{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 2 ({{ill|1869|en|1869|qid=Q7720|lt=1869|1=1869}}) saw the enshrinement of the {{ill|Bunrei|en|Bunrei|qid=Q195793|lt=Bunrei|1=Bunrei}} from the head office – {{ill|Corporate headquarters|en|Corporate headquarters|qid=Q1530704|lt=General Head Office|1=Corporate headquarters}} – of {{ill|Kurume Suitengū|en|Kurume Suitengū|qid=Q3200625|lt=Kurume Suitengu|1=Kurume Suitengū}}, which was combined ({{ill|合祀|1=co-Enshrinement|2=ja|3=合祀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/合祀|13=User:Immanuelle/co-Enshrinement|qq=}}) with the Inari Shrine ({{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|qid=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine|1=Inari shrine}}) and Yaken Shrine (弥剣神社（{{ill|Gion Shrine|ja|祇園社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祇園神社|1=Gion shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588442}}）) within the area to establish the shrine. In addition, the Inari Shrine was founded in {{ill|Bunroku|en|Bunroku|qid=Q1373039|lt=Bunroku|1=Bunroku}} 3 ({{ill|1587|en|1587|qid=Q6744|lt=1587|1=1587}}) by {{ill|Tachibana Muneshige|en|Tachibana Muneshige|qid=Q1071770|lt=Tachibana Muneshige|1=Tachibana Muneshige}}, while the Yaken Shrine was established during the {{ill|Bunka|en|Bunka|qid=Q1373146|lt=Bunka|1=Bunka}} period (1804–1818).
Locally, it is known as "'''Suitengu-san'''". During the Okinohata Suitengu Festival held on May 3, 4, and 5, a boat stage called Sangu-maru is constructed and the Suitengu festival music is performed from dusk.
== 祭事 ==
* 2月初午日 初午祭
* 5月3～5日 水天宮大祭
* 7月20・21日 祇園祭
== Access ==
* {{ill|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|en|Nishi-Nippon Railroad|qid=Q869251|lt=Nishitetsu|1=Nishi-Nippon Railroad}}{{ill|Nishitetsu Tenjin Ōmuta Line|en|Nishitetsu Tenjin Ōmuta Line|qid=Q901075|lt=Tenjin Ōmuta Line|1=Nishitetsu Tenjin Ōmuta Line}}{{ill|Nishitetsu Yanagawa Station|en|Nishitetsu Yanagawa Station|qid=Q11629907|lt=Yanagawa Station|1=Nishitetsu Yanagawa Station}} – alight and then:
** Board the {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|1=Nishitetsu Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11629843}} bound for "Hayatsue" ("早津江"), alight at the "Suitengu Entrance" ("水天宮入口") bus stop; a 4-minute walk.
** Alternatively, take the same bus bound for "Hayatsue" or the "Yanagawa Hospital Loop" ("柳川病院循環"), alight at the "Mihanae" ("御花前") bus stop; a 6-minute walk.
** Board the {{ill|Horikawa Bus|ja|堀川バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Horikawa Bus|1=Horikawa Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11427415}} bound for "Kanpo no Yado Yanagawa" ("かんぽの宿柳川"), alight at the final stop; an 8-minute walk.
** Approximately 10 minutes by taxi from the station.
